title: helm(private): validate encryption + nodeAffinity in private values init hooks
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add validation for encryption configuration and nodeAffinity/tolerations in private Helm chart values; improve init-hook stability during upgrades and provide clearer upgrade/rollback compatibility notes.
description: Context: private deployments require stricter validation of Helm values to avoid silent misconfigurations during upgrade/rollback and to ensure encryption and node placement settings are respected by init hooks. This PR adds a values schema, runtime validation in the init job, and templating fixes to keep upgrade/rollback behavior stable. Motivation: several customer upgrades surfaced two classes of issues: (1) missing KMS/encryption config causing init jobs to create unencrypted secrets; (2) nodeAffinity/toleration fields ignored by the init hook leading to pods scheduled on incorrect nodes during upgrades. Changes in this PR: - values.schema.json for charts/redwood-private: new validation for encryption.kmsKey, encryption.enabled, and placement.nodeAffinity/tolerations. - templates/init-job.yaml: runtime checks that fail fast if required encryption fields are missing; uses helm tpl/lookup to populate KMS secrets and respects .Values.placement.* when creating temporary pods. - templates/_helpers.tpl: helper functions for safe boolean parsing, env rendering for encryption config, and stable naming to ensure upgrade-safe resource names. - Chart.yaml bump and README private/upgrade notes updated with guidance on rolling upgrades and rollback implications. - tests/helm: added unit tests validating schema rejection and basic helm template output for nodeAffinity and encryption envs. Checklist: [x] values schema defined and included in chart package, [x] init job respects values.placement and fails fast on encryption misconfig, [x] automated tests added, [x] docs updated (upgrade/rollback notes). Related: ENG-1294 (upgrade stability), SUP-9821 (customer incident reproduced).

review_comments: Ethan Wong: Please ensure the init job error messages are actionable for operators (e.g., indicate exactly which field is missing).
Maya Patel: Updated init job to exit with explicit messages and GUID-like error codes for support correlation.
Priya Singh: Can we avoid creating new CRD-level changes here to keep upgrades non-breaking?
Maya Patel: No CRD changes. All validation is at Helm/schema/init-job runtime layer so older clusters can still upgrade; documented any edge cases in upgrade-rollback.md.
Liam O'Connor: CI flaked on helm unit tests first run, seen a template rendering order issue with tpl/lookup. Can you add a retry to the test?
Maya Patel: Added deterministic rendering helpers and retried the flaky test; CI green on rerun.
